_authority: AUTHORED. Silence is not permission: startup_policy.check() refuses any observed mechanism this file does not classify.
_purpose: Classify every startup mechanism that can influence the graded assurance run, and bind the content of every one that is allowed.
_why_this_file_exists: Gate 4N-I28AF finding ADV-I28AF-02: the startup surface was recorded as evidence and never adjudicated, so a staged sitecustomize.py was accepted while every executed module stayed byte-identical.

BASH_ENV.why_prohibited: sourced by non-interactive bash, so it executes inside the CI wrapper scripts that reach the graded command

PATH.failure_behavior: refuse if a required executable is unresolvable
PATH.why_allowed: the assurance chain shells out to git and bash; both are system executables by design

PYTEST_ADDOPTS.why_prohibited: injects arbitrary pytest flags into the graded command without editing it; Gate 4N-I28AF used exactly this to drop four assurance modules from collection

PYTEST_PLUGINS.why_prohibited: loads plugins the pinned command never names

PYTHONHOME.why_prohibited: relocates the standard library, which would change which code every import resolves to

PYTHONPATH.failure_behavior: refuse any entry outside the repository trust root, and any repository entry other than scripts/
PYTHONPATH.why_allowed: the graded command sets PYTHONPATH=<workspace>/scripts so the protected modules are importable as -p plugins; this is the pinned invocation, not an injection

PYTHONSTARTUP.why_not_applicable: CPython reads PYTHONSTARTUP only in interactive mode. Measured: with PYTHONSTARTUP pointing at a file that raises SystemExit, `python -m pytest --version` and `python -c` both run normally and the file does not execute, while `python -i` does read it. The graded command is non-interactive, so this variable cannot influence it — and refusing it would break every operator shell that legitimately sets one for the REPL.

conftest.failure_behavior: refuse an unpinned conftest, a missing pinned conftest, or changed content
conftest.scope: the collection roots the graded `pytest tests/` invocation actually reaches: the repository root and tests/. Vendored conftests inside .venv/node_modules are excluded because that run never loads them.
conftest.why_allowed: pytest requires conftest for fixture and collection wiring; a conftest executes during collection and can remove tests, so every one is pinned by content

import_hooks_meta_path.why_not_applicable: Gate 4N-I28AC measured that pytest inserts its AssertionRewritingHook at meta_path[0] AFTER sitecustomize runs, displacing an attacker finder; the substitution that does work is sys.modules pre-seeding, which executed-code and executed-state provenance bind directly. Recorded so a future change to that measurement is a visible policy decision.

interpreter_site_flags.why_not_applicable: -S/-I would DISABLE site loading, which can only remove startup mechanisms, never add one; the prohibited-mechanism checks above already refuse anything site loading could introduce.

pth_files.why_prohibited: a .pth line beginning with import executes at site initialisation, earlier than any assurance code can observe

pytest_plugins.failure_behavior: refuse a plugin module loaded from outside the repository or the interpreter installation
pytest_plugins.why_allowed: the graded command names -p signalnest_bootstrap and -p pytest_session_guard, and pytest loads its own machinery; all must resolve inside the trust root

sitecustomize.why_prohibited: the exact ACC-I28AC-01 vector: auto-imported at interpreter startup from the graded command's own PYTHONPATH, before pytest exists, and able to pre-seed sys.modules

usercustomize.why_prohibited: same mechanism as sitecustomize, sourced from user-site instead of PYTHONPATH
